title: Bayes' Theorem: Updating Beliefs with Evidence
pedagogical_goal: This simulation demonstrates how Bayes' Theorem updates prior beliefs about hypotheses (e.g., which bag a marble came from) when new evidence (e.g., observing a red marble) is presented. Users manipulate prior probabilities and likelihoods to see how the posterior probability changes in real-time, reinforcing the relationship between conditional probability and evidence-based belief revision.

fundamental_laws: Bayes' Theorem: P(H|E) = [P(E|H) * P(H)] / P(E), where P(E) = P(E|H)*P(H) + P(E|¬H)*P(¬H)
Conditional Probability: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B)
Law of Total Probability: P(E) = Σ [P(E|H_i) * P(H_i)] for all mutually exclusive hypotheses H_i

Filled with accent color, stroke primary. Contains 7 red circles (radius 8px) and 3 black circles (radius 8px) to visually represent the marble composition based on likelihood_red_given_left.

A stylized bag silhouette on the right (x=780, y=240) defined by a curved SVG path: starts at (750,200), curves to (720,280), then to (780,320), to (840,280), and back to (750,200). Filled with accent color, stroke primary. Contains 3 red circles (radius 8px) and 7 black circles (radius 8px) to visually represent the marble composition based on likelihood_red_given_right.

A single red marble (circle, radius 12px) that appears at the bottom center (x=480, y=420) when evidence is observed. It pulses with a glow effect (using accent color and glow) to draw attention. Initially hidden (opacity 0), becomes visible (opacity 1) when simulation starts, representing the observed evidence (drawing a red marble).

A dynamic curved ribbon (cubic Bezier) flowing from the left bag to the evidence marble, then splitting to show posterior. Path: M180,240 C250,180 400,180 480,420 (to marble), then splits: M480,420 C520,380 580,380 620,300 (to posterior display). Stroke width varies with joint_red_left value, colored with primary color and 60% opacity. Represents the flow of probability mass from left bag hypothesis to evidence and then to posterior.

Path: M780,240 C710,180 560,180 480,420 (to marble), then splits: M480,420 C440,380 380,380 340,300 (to posterior display). Stroke width varies with joint_red_right value, colored with secondary color and 60% opacity. Represents the flow of probability mass from right bag hypothesis to evidence and then to posterior.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Setting the Priors
pedagogical_callouts.text: Begin by establishing your initial beliefs: what is the probability the marble came from the left bag before seeing any evidence? This is P(Left). The right bag gets the remaining probability: P(Right) = 1 - P(Left).

pedagogical_callouts.title: Introducing the Evidence
pedagogical_callouts.text: Now, observe the evidence: a red marble is drawn. How likely is this evidence under each hypothesis? P(Red|Left) and P(Red|Right) represent these likelihoods. The joint probability P(Red ∩ Left) = P(Left) * P(Red|Left) quantifies the chance of both the hypothesis and evidence occurring together.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Updating Beliefs via Bayes' Theorem
pedagogical_callouts.text: Bayes' Theorem normalizes the joint probabilities by the total evidence probability: P(Left|Red) = P(Red ∩ Left) / P(Red). The posterior probability tells us our updated belief that the marble came from the left bag after seeing the red evidence. Notice how changing likelihoods or priors shifts the posterior.

pedagogical_callouts.title: The Role of Total Evidence
pedagogical_callouts.text: The denominator P(Red) = P(Red∩Left) + P(Red∩Right) ensures the posterior probabilities sum to 1. It represents the overall chance of observing a red marble from either bag. If one bag is much more likely to produce red, it dominates the posterior even with a modest prior.
